source: zen's own Plex Media Server 1.42.2.10156-f737b826c (claimed by the account, the version plexsim reports): its log, read on disk; and plex.tv's live answer to the same GET for plexsim-e2e (machine aebd096f...), asked with plexsim-e2e's own server token and PMS's headers
note: Tokens are replaced: SERVER-TOKEN is the asking server's own token (its own device row heads the list), ACCOUNT-TOKEN the account token a client of this server holds (the resource's accessToken for an owned server is the asking client's own token, and it is one of these rows), DEVICE-TOKEN-n every other device of the owner. IPs are redacted. The request a real PMS sends is recorded in plextv_registration_s1422.json (claimed_start, GET /api/v2/server/access_tokens): PMS's thirteen headers plus X-Plex-Token, auth_token=<server token> in the query.

refresh_census.window: Oct 10 03:29-07:44 UTC, three rotated log files
refresh_census.fetches: 586 access_tokens requests logged for 604 'Refreshing tokens' lines
refresh_census.reading: a token the server does not hold makes it re-read the list unless the last read FINISHED (access_tokens, then server/users) about 6 s ago or less: no refresh started sooner than 5.68 s after the previous one's server/users answer, and no 'recently enough' came later than 5.86 s after one. Counted from the START of a refresh it is not a window: two 'recently enough' lines came 7.9 s after a refresh started, 0.13 s after its slow server/users answer. Nothing re-reads the list on a timer: the hour after the probe's claimed restart has no further read (plextv_registration_s1422.json steady_state), and a claimed start reads it first (claimed_start).
